content.text:
Let me analyze the situation.

Stark round 5, place orders. Occupied regions: bay-of-ice (ship), castle-black (2 knights), karhold (1 knight), winterfell (1 footman), the-narrow-sea (1 ship). maxStarredOrders: 0, so no starred tokens. Raid restricted.

I'm at 1 VP, need to expand. Goal: capture castles.

Available undefended castles reachable:
- From Castle Black: Flint's Finger (land castle, but is it reachable? Castle Black neighbours: bay-of-ice, karhold, the-shivering-sea, winterfell. Flint's Finger is not directly adjacent to Castle Black. Hmm. Actually the tool said "From Castle Black, the current land connections and friendly Ships reach these undefended castle areas you do not own: Flint's Finger." That uses ship transport maybe. Castle Black isn't coastal... Bay of Ice is adjacent to Flint's Finger. So knights from Castle Black can't move to sea. Hmm, land units can't move into sea. Castle Black -> bay-of-ice is sea, not traversable by land units unless... no. Actually ship transport: land units move between coastal areas connected by sea areas with friendly ships. Castle Black is not coastal (no sea adjacency except via... castle-black is adjacent to bay-of-ice and the-shivering-sea which are seas). Hmm, castle-black neighbours include the-shivering-sea (sea) and bay-of-ice (sea). So Castle Black may be coastal! Land units departing from a coastal area connected by friendly ships.

Bay of Ice has a Stark ship. So from Castle Black (coastal? it's adjacent to bay-of-ice sea), ships in bay-of-ice connect Castle Black to Flint's Finger? Flint's Finger is adjacent to bay-of-ice. So ship transport: Castle Black -> bay-of-ice -> Flint's Finger. Yes, land units can march from Castle Black to Flint's Finger via ship transport.

Actually ship transport requires the land areas be connected by consecutive sea areas each containing friendly ships. Castle Black adjacent to bay-of-ice (friendly ship), and Flint's Finger adjacent to bay-of-ice. So yes, Castle Black -> Flint's Finger is a legal ship-transport march.

Flint's Finger is a castle (castle=1), undefended currently (greyjoy control power token but no units). Wait flints-finger controlPowerToken greyjoy, no units. Marching into an area with only enemy power token: no combat, power token discarded, take control. So capturing Flint's Finger requires marching a land unit there.

From Winterfell: Moat Cailin, White Harbor reachable by land (winterfell neighbours: moat-cailin, white-harbor etc.). Both undefended? moat-cailin castle=1, white-harbor castle=1. Let me check current board: moat-cailin not listed in board (no units), white-harbor not listed. They're likely empty, controlled by no one (no power token). So a single unit can march there and take control.

So I have several March opportunities. Winterfell has 1 footman. If it marches out, Winterfell reverts to me due to home area (no power token needed). So march the footman from Winterfell to Moat Cailin or White Harbor. But then Winterfell still counts as mine (home). Good.

Castle Black has 2 knights, Karhold has 1 knight.

Plan: March orders on Winterfell (to take Moat Cailin/White Harbor), Castle Black (to take Flint's Finger), Karhold (maybe support or march). Also I should consolidate power for tokens (I have 3 power tokens, supply 1).

Supply 1: permitted army sizes 3,2. I have armies? castle-black 2 knights = army of 2 (ok, size 2). Others single units. Fine.

Actually let me think about which regions need orders.

We have 5 occupied regions and must assign exactly 5 orders. maxStarred 0.

Regions:
1. bay-of-ice (ship) - sea. Consolidate power on sea earns nothing. Options: support, defense (no effect in sea? Defense order on sea... sea areas can be attacked, defense works). Actually to support adjacent battles, support on ship is useful. But there are no battles nearby likely. Could give raid? raid restricted anyway. Actually I need to think about what's useful.

2. castle-black (2 knights) - want march to capture Flint's Finger.
3. karhold (1 knight) - could march or support.
4. winterfell (1 footman) - march to capture Moat Cailin or White Harbor.
5. the-narrow-sea (ship) - support.

But wait, bay-of-ice ship is needed for ship transport from Castle Black to Flint's Finger. Ship transport works regardless of order token on the ship (rules: "Ship units can facilitate ship transport regardless of the type of Order token currently assigned to their sea area."). So I can put support/defense on bay-of-ice and it still transports. Good.

However, if I want to capture multiple castles, I can only get one per March order area. Castle Black march -> Flint's Finger. Winterfell march -> Moat Cailin. Karhold march -> ? Karhold neighbours: castle-black, the-shivering-sea, winterfell. No castle reachable directly except via... Karhold land units: neighbours castle-black (mine), winterfell (mine), the-shivering-sea(sea). No enemy castle adjacent. So Karhold knight could support or move.

Actually to capture 2 castles this round (Flint's Finger, Moat Cailin), I need two march orders. That gives VP potentially 1+2 = 3.

Wait, current VP=1 (Winterfell stronghold). Castle Black and Karhold are crown icons, contribute 0 castle. So capturing Flint's Finger and Moat Cailin would add 2 → VP 3.

White Harbor is also a castle reachable from Winterfell. And Moat Cailin. Both undefended. But only one march from Winterfell (one area). Could also use Karhold knight to take White Harbor? Karhold not adjacent to white harbor.

Hmm, could Winterfell footman march to White Harbor via ship transport from the-shivering-sea? The-shivering-sea... do I have ships there? No. Bay of Ice ship. White Harbor is adjacent to the-narrow-sea and port-of-white-harbor, the-shivering-sea. I have a ship in the-narrow-sea. White Harbor is adjacent to the-narrow-sea (sea). So ship transport via the-narrow-sea connects Winterfell? Winterfell is adjacent to bay-of-ice, port-of-winterfell, the-shivering-sea, the-stony-shore, moat-cailin, white-harbor, castle-black, karhold. Winterfell directly adjacent to white-harbor (land), so just march by land.

So from Winterfell I could march to Moat Cailin OR White Harbor OR both? One march order moves units to one or more adjacent areas, but only one combat per march. Both Moat Cailin and White Harbor are empty (no combat needed). "For each March Order, a player may move units into only one area containing units of another House." Since no enemy units, can I split movement into multiple empty areas? "Units may move together or separately into several adjacent areas." Winterfell has only 1 footman though. So one unit to one area.

Hmm, but I want to take both Moat Cailin and White Harbor eventually. This round take one.

Let's prioritize: which castles are most valuable/defensible? Moat Cailin (castle=1) at the neck; White Harbor (castle=1) near Winterfell.

Actually think about supply: Moat Cailin no supply, White Harbor no supply. Flint's Finger no supply.

Given I want max castles, and opponents: Greyjoy has seagard with 2 knights and greywater-watch footman, flints-finger power token. Greyjoy is a threat to the north. Martell/Lannister strong.

I also should consider that marching out of Castle Black toward Flint's Finger exposes? Flint's Finger is on the western coast near Greyjoy (greyjoy has flints-finger power token, ironmans-bay). Actually Greyjoy could contest.

Let me think about the best plan. I have limited power (3). Capturing empty castles doesn't need power. Leaving areas: Winterfell home stays mine. Castle Black: if I march both knights out to Flint's Finger, Castle Black becomes vacant and I'd lose control unless I leave a power token (costs 1 power) — but Castle Black contributes 0 castle VP, though it's a land area/crown. Hmm, but I'd rather not vacate it fully. Keep 1 knight there and send 1 knight to Flint's Finger? A single knight marching to Flint's Finger: no combat there (empty), fine. Marching 1 knight from Castle Black to Flint's Finger via ship transport needs bay-of-ice ship (friendly). Good. But can a single knight move via ship transport into a coastal area? Yes.

Actually wait—do I even need ship transport? Castle Black to Flint's Finger direct: are they adjacent? Castle Black neighbours: bay-of-ice, karhold, the-shivering-sea, winterfell. Not flints-finger. So ship transport needed via bay-of-ice.

Alternatively from Winterfell, Flint's Finger isn't adjacent either (winterfell neighbours don't include flints-finger).

OK so Castle Black knight -> Flint's Finger.

Now, could I also march from bay-of-ice ship somewhere? Ships can move to adjacent seas.

Let me design 5 orders:
- winterfell: march (to take Moat Cailin or White Harbor) - priority high
- castle-black: march (knight to Flint's Finger) - priority high
- karhold: support or defense or march
- bay-of-ice: support (to support adjacent combat) or consolidate (no power at sea, so pointless) - support or defense
- the-narrow-sea: support/defense

Since no battles are likely to occur (undefended castles), support/defense are marginal. But raids are restricted.

Hmm, but defense on castle-black would prevent march. I want marches on winterfell and castle-black.

What about consolidating power for power tokens? I have 3 power tokens, supply 1. Consolidate Power on land areas with power icons gives tokens. Which of my regions have power icons (crowns)? castle-black crown=1, karhold crown=1, winterfell crown=1. So consolidate power on castle-black/karhold/winterfell would give 1 + crown count. But I want to march from those. Only one order per area.

I could put consolidate_power on karhold (gives 1 + 1 = 2 power? Actually Consolidate Power: 1 power + 1 per power icon. Crown icons count as power icons? The card "Game of Thrones" says power icons. On board, areas have "crown" values which are power icons for consolidate power). So karhold crown=1 → 2 power. That helps build reserves.

But wait, if I don't march with karhold knight, it stays and defends. Fine.

Priority: The useful actions are the two marches. Then karhold consolidate power for tokens. Then bay-of-ice and the-narrow-sea support (or defense).

But the harness only allocates tokens based on availability; there are two support tokens (7,8) and one starred support (9, not allowed). Two regular marches (1: -1, 2: +0). Starred march (3) not allowed since maxStarred 0. So two march tokens available. Good, exactly two marches.

Consolidate power: two regular (10, 11). Support: two regular (7,8). Defense: two regular (4,5).

So I can assign: winterfell march (+0 ideally, priority high so gets token 2), castle-black march (gets token 1, -1... hmm). Actually the harness preserves category preference but the modifier assignment depends on priority: higher priority gets stronger March modifier. So higher priority should be the one where combat bonus matters. Flint's Finger has no combat, Moat Cailin no combat. Modifier doesn't matter for empty captures. So assign priority to whichever.

Let me set:
- winterfell: march, priority 100 (take Moat Cailin — closer to south, blocks Greyjoy expansion) 
- castle-black: march, priority 90 (take Flint's Finger)
- karhold: consolidate_power, priority 80
- the-narrow-sea: support, priority 50
- bay-of-ice: support, priority 40

Hmm, but maybe better: use the-narrow-sea ship to support? There's no battle near. Alternatively defense on the ships to protect from naval attack. Greyjoy has ships in ironmans-bay, port-of-pyke. Could Greyjoy attack bay-of-ice? Greyjoy ironmans-bay ship could move to sunset-sea/bay-of-ice. Possibly. Defense order on bay-of-ice would give defense bonus if attacked. But support token gives no defense. Hmm.

Actually is defending my sea important? The bay-of-ice ship is my transport link to Flint's Finger. If Greyjoy takes bay-of-ice, I lose transport and the ship. Defense +1 there might help. But Greyjoy has 1 ship in ironmans-bay; to reach bay-of-ice it must go via sunset-sea (ironmans-bay -> sunset-sea -> bay-of-ice, two moves). So not this round likely.

Let me consider raids: restricted, so ignore.

Also consider: could a support order be useful to support my own march combats? Not needed since empty.

I think defense orders on the two ships might be more useful than support (no battles to support). Actually defense on a ship in sea: if attacked, bonus. Support has zero value with no adjacent combat. But if I march into a castle and an opponent attacks later in the round... no, combat only when I attack or they attack. Support order helps only in declared combats. There could be combats elsewhere adjacent to my ships (e.g., Greyjoy attacking seagard? not adjacent to my areas). Hmm.

I'll go with defense on the two sea areas to protect the ships/transport, OR support. Let me think: The prompt says "Use Defence or Support when you have a concrete battle to protect or assist; otherwise these orders can leave an army unable to expand." Ships can't take land castles anyway, so sea orders are just defensive/support. Defense on bay-of-ice protects transport. I'll pick defense for bay-of-ice (protects Flint's Finger link), support for the-narrow-sea (could support White Harbor defense if attacked, or support an adjacent battle). Actually support on the-narrow-sea could support Moat Cailin or White Harbor if attacked from sea? Support from sea to land: ship units may support adjacent combat in a sea or land area. So the-narrow-sea ship can support Moat Cailin? Is moat-cailin adjacent to the-narrow-sea? Yes (moat-cailin neighbours: the-narrow-sea). So if I capture Moat Cailin and it's attacked, support from the-narrow-sea helps. Good. So support on the-narrow-sea makes sense if I march to Moat Cailin.

Similarly bay-of-ice ship can support Flint's Finger? flints-finger neighbours: bay-of-ice, greywater-watch, ironmans-bay, sunset-sea. Yes bay-of-ice adjacent. So support from bay-of-ice could defend Flint's Finger. Hmm.

Maybe both should be support to defend newly captured castles. But defense on bay-of-ice also good. Let me consider: which is more likely—attack on Flint's Finger (Greyjoy from seagard/greywater-watch) or attack on Moat Cailin (from seagard/moat? Greyjoy has greywater-watch footman adjacent to moat-cailin? greywater-watch neighbours: moat-cailin yes). 

I'll set both sea areas to support, since support helps defend land castles I capture and can also help in sea battles. Actually defense only helps the defended area (the sea area itself). Support helps adjacent land battles. Given I'm capturing land castles, support is better.

But note support token priority: harness has only two regular support tokens. Both sea areas want support. Good.

Priority ordering: Let me make the two marches high priority (100, 90), then consolidate power karhold (80), then supports (60, 50). Actually for token allocation, the harness assigns categories per preference. Since two support tokens exist and both sea areas want support, fine.

Should Winterfell march +0 (token 2) or the castle-black? Doesn't matter for combat. But higher priority gets stronger march modifier. Assign winterfell priority 100 → gets March +0 (token 2). castle-black priority 90 → gets March -1 (token 1). Fine.

Wait, actually is karhold consolidate power better than a third march? Karhold knight can't reach any castle. Could Karhold knight march to reinforce? It could march to castle-black to join (staging) or to winterfell. Not needed. Consolidate power gives power tokens which are valuable for bidding (I have only 3). Good.

Actually, an important consideration: this round might have a Westeros card that matters. Round 5. Not sure. We just place orders.

Let me reconsider whether to march from Winterfell to Moat Cailin or White Harbor. Moat Cailin is a castle at the neck; White Harbor is a castle near Winterfell. Both good. Moat Cailin more strategic (blocks south). But is Moat Cailin maybe contested by Greyjoy (seagard knight adjacent)? Greyjoy has seagard with 2 knights; moat-cailin adjacent to seagard. If I leave only 1 footman in Moat Cailin, Greyjoy could take it. Hmm. White Harbor less contested (adjacent to widows-watch, the-shivering-sea, moat-cailin, winterfell, port). Neutral-ish.

Alternatively, march Winterfell footman to White Harbor (safe), and later take Moat Cailin. Hmm.

Actually, I could send BOTH the footman from Winterfell and something to Moat Cailin? No, one area one march.

Let me think about which is safer and which gives more. Both are castle=1 (1 VP). Moat Cailin has a castle and is a chokepoint. White Harbor also castle. 

I think capturing Moat Cailin is high value but risky. White Harbor safe. Let me capture White Harbor this round with Winterfell footman (safe), and keep Moat Cailin as a target later. Actually wait—if Greyjoy grabs Moat Cailin next, that's bad. But I can't do everything.

Alternatively: Karhold knight could march to... castle-black, then... no.

Hmm, another thought: Winterfell footman to Moat Cailin, and the-narrow-sea ship supports. Also I could later take White Harbor. Greyjoy might attack Moat Cailin though.

Let me evaluate Greyjoy's likely moves. Greyjoy has 8 power. Greyjoy regions: pyke, ironmans-bay, port-of-pyke, seagard (2 knights), flints-finger (token), greywater-watch (footman). Greyjoy is expanding in the north. They likely will attack flints-finger? They already control it via token. They might move seagard knights to moat-cailin or greywater-watch footman to moat-cailin. Or attack winterfell region? Greyjoy could be aggressive.

Given Greyjoy presence, Flint's Finger capture by me will likely be contested. Hmm.

Honestly any plan has risk. Let me maximize: capture Flint's Finger (from Castle Black) and White Harbor (from Winterfell), both relatively safe/close, and consolidate power at Karhold for tokens.

Actually wait, Flint's Finger: Greyjoy has a power token there but no units; greywater-watch footman is adjacent. If I march 1 knight into flints-finger, I take it. But Greyjoy could then counterattack from greywater-watch (1 footman vs 1 knight: Greyjoy attacker 1 + card; I defend 1 knight = 2 + card). Likely holds. And bay-of-ice ship could support my defense.

Let me finalize: 
- winterfell: march, priority 100 → White Harbor (safe)
- castle-black: march, priority 95 → Flint's Finger (knight via ship transport)
- karhold: consolidate_power, priority 70
- the-narrow-sea: support, priority 60
- bay-of-ice: support, priority 55

Hmm, but support tokens: only two regular support (7,8). Both use support. Good.

Actually maybe defense on bay-of-ice to protect the ship that is critical for Flint's Finger transport? If bay-of-ice ship is attacked and lost, Flint's Finger becomes hard to hold. But Greyjoy's nearest ship is ironmans-bay (2 moves away). Low risk this round. Support better.

Let me double check: can support order be placed on a sea area and be useful? Yes.

Also the prompt hints: "Consolidate Power in an open sea earns no power" — so don't do that. Good.

Wait, one more: could I gain more castles by marching from Castle Black with both knights splitting? One to Flint's Finger, but only one area can receive units if it's the only combat. Both knights to same area fine. I'll move both knights to Flint's Finger? Then Castle Black vacant and I lose it (0 castle VP anyway, but it's a land area with crown and defensible position). Better keep 1 knight at Castle Black. But Castle Black with 1 knight and no order... wait, castle-black gets a march order; if I only move 1 of 2 knights, the other stays, so no vacating. Good, no power token needed.

Actually, can I move both knights and leave Castle Black? Then Castle Black would be lost unless power token. It contributes 0 VP but a land area and staging. Keep 1 knight.

Hmm, but actually moving both knights to Flint's Finger gives a stronger defense (2 knights = 4 str). Flint's Finger is more exposed. But losing Castle Black (safe rear) isn't great. I'll keep one knight at Castle Black.

Wait, but if I move only 1 knight, Castle Black still has 1 knight, and the march order token is on castle-black. Fine.

Alternatively, move 1 knight to Flint's Finger and the other knight could... no, only one combat/multiple empty areas. Could split to different empty areas? Flint's Finger only castle nearby. Keep it simple.

Final answer with priorities. Let me also consider starred: maxStarred 0, so starred_preference "avoid" everywhere.

Let me write the assignments.

Actually, reconsider: Should karhold get march to support castle-black or move? No. Consolidate power is good for power tokens. Keep.

Let me reconsider "the-narrow-sea support": the-narrow-sea ship adjacent to moat-cailin, white-harbor, the-shivering-sea, widows-watch, the-eyrie, the-fingers, the-mountains-of-the-moon, crackclaw-point, port-of-white-harbor, the-twins. So it could support White Harbor if attacked. Good. Set support priority 60.

bay-of-ice support: adjacent to flints-finger, winterfell, castle-black, the-stony-shore, greywater-watch, sunset-sea. Supports Flint's Finger. Good.

I'll submit.

Let me quickly verify with check_neighbours maybe not necessary. I'm fairly confident.

Actually, one concern: the prompt says "A single land unit can capture an empty castle with a March order." Castle Black knight moving to Flint's Finger requires ship transport through bay-of-ice which has my ship. The ship has a support/defense order but transport works regardless. Good.

But wait: Is Castle Black coastal such that land units can depart via ship transport? Ship transport: "Any two land areas are considered adjacent for the purposes of marching... when they are connected by consecutive sea areas (or a single sea area) each containing one or more friendly Ship units." Castle Black is a land area adjacent to bay-of-ice (sea). Flint's Finger is a land area adjacent to bay-of-ice (sea). So they are connected by a single sea area (bay-of-ice) containing a friendly ship. So yes, legal. 

Now submit.

Priorities: winterfell 100, castle-black 90, karhold 70, the-narrow-sea 60, bay-of-ice 50.

I'll also save strategy note? Only after final accepted. The remember_strategy queues note after final action accepted. I can call it before submitting. Optional. Let me include a brief plan update.

Actually the instruction: "remember_strategy records a proposed update... saved only after your final action is accepted." I can call it. Let me do it to keep plan fresh. But I should focus; it's helpful.

Let me just submit orders and optionally remember strategy. I'll call remember_strategy then submit final JSON.

I'll write the note quickly.

actionOutputSchema.description: You are placing planning orders for this round. Assign an order preference to each required occupied area, respecting the displayed restrictions and starred-order limit. Your final answer submits the whole order draft and marks your house ready. These orders determine what your armies can do later; this decision does not move units. A single land unit can capture an empty castle with a March order. Defence and Support orders do not move that unit or claim neighbouring land. Consolidate Power in an open sea earns no power; a port follows the separate port rule. The harness allocates the physical order tokens, preserving higher-priority preferences when not all requested categories fit the available tokens. Priority 100 is most important; 0 is least important. Plan how to gain castle areas this round. Use Defence or Support when you have a concrete battle to protect or assist; otherwise these orders can leave an army unable to expand.
